risk_free_rate.source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (H.15), Market Yield on U.S. Treasury Securities at 3-Month Constant Maturity, Quoted on an Investment Basis (DGS3MO), via FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS3MO (read 2026-09-28)

strategy.name: Timing: baseline, short decided on bar 1 (10:00)

rules.action: Enter the long on the first bar of the session where the condition holds. Decide the short only on session bar {bar} of the week-open session (bar 1 ends at 10:00): sell it if the condition holds there, or else G-1 skips the week
rules.condition: The selected contract has a valid bid and ask, and its spread is at most {long_max_spread:.0%} of mid for the long leg or {short_max_spread:.0%} for the short leg
rules.name: Entry trigger, fixed bar
rules.rationale: The entry-timing check: the baseline with E-T1's liquidity trigger replaced by a fixed bar of the week-open session, run once for each of its bars. Large dispersion in results across the bars is reported as fragility.

rules.action: Buy the E-L2 and E-L3 selection when E-T1 passes. If it doesn't pass this session, retry each following session until it does
rules.condition: No long call is held: the window's first session, or a session in which X-L1 or X-L2 sold it
rules.name: Long leg timing
rules.rationale: The long call is bought on the first day of the backtest. If no bar in a session passes E-T1, the entry is retried the next session.

rules.action: Choose the monthly expiry nearest {target_dte} days to expiry
rules.condition: Monthly expiries listed at the decision bar
rules.name: Long leg expiry
rules.rationale: The textbook PMCC long: a monthly about {target_dte} days out. A listed option with 9 months or less to expiry has no loan value under Reg T, so the long is always fully paid.

rules.action: Choose the strike with delta nearest {target_delta:.2f}
rules.condition: Eligible calls on the E-L2 expiry
rules.name: Long leg strike
rules.rationale: The long call is the stock substitute: a deep in-the-money, long-dated call, here at the textbook PMCC's delta of {target_delta:.2f}.

rules.action: Buy a fixed quantity of {contracts}. No entry, logged, if it would make available funds negative. Every account starts with {cash_multiple}× the most expensive first long-leg cost in the universe, rounded up to the nearest ${cash_round_to:,.0f}
rules.condition: Every long entry
rules.name: Sizing
rules.rationale: One long call and one short call. Every symbol's account starts with the same cash balance, used for NAV and Reg T tracking, and no entry is made that would make available funds negative.

rules.action: Sell a new short call; E-T1 decides which bar
rules.condition: Each Monday (the first session of the week if Monday is a holiday), while a long call is held and no short is open
rules.name: Short leg timing
rules.rationale: One short call a week, sold as the week opens. A short closed early isn't replaced until the next Monday, so every new short passes the skip-week gates.

rules.action: Use the expiry on that week's final trading session
rules.condition: Selling the week's short call
rules.name: Short leg expiry
rules.rationale: The short lives for one week. Its expiry is the week's last trading session, so a holiday week never gets an invented Friday expiry: when the Friday is a holiday, it expires on Thursday.

rules.action: Choose the strike with delta nearest {target_delta:.2f}
rules.condition: Eligible out-of-the-money calls on the E-S2 expiry
rules.name: Short leg strike
rules.rationale: The textbook PMCC short: a weekly call out of the money at a fixed delta. If the selected strike fails E-T1 or E-S5, the skip-week gates decide; no other strike is substituted.

rules.action: Sell as many contracts as the long leg holds
rules.condition: Selling the week's short call
rules.name: Short leg quantity
rules.rationale: Each short call is covered by one long call with a lower strike and a later expiry, so the position is a diagonal spread and the short needs no margin of its own under Reg T.

rules.action: Sell the short only if this holds; otherwise G-2 skips the week
rules.condition: Short strike − long strike > long entry fill − short mid, per share
rules.name: Structural constraint
rules.rationale: The gap between the strikes has to be bigger than the net debit paid. Then, if the short finishes deep in the money, the long leg's intrinsic gain covers the short's loss plus the debit, so the trade still doesn't lose money overall. It uses the long leg's entry fill, not its current mark, which keeps it conservative.

rules.action: Skip the week; keep the long
rules.condition: Selected short never passes E-T1 on any Monday bar
rules.name: No quote / liquidity
rules.rationale: No tradable quote, no trade: the backtest never invents a fill and never swaps in a different strike. G-1 replaces a separate short-leg spread gate, since E-T1's spread threshold already covers it.

rules.action: Skip the week; keep the long
rules.condition: Selected short fails E-S5
rules.name: Structural constraint
rules.rationale: A short that could turn the position into a net loss isn't sold, and no other strike is tried in its place.

rules.action: Buy to close at mid. No new short until next Monday
rules.condition: Short mid ≤ {max_credit_fraction:.0%} of the credit received, on any bar before the Friday check
rules.name: Take profit
rules.rationale:
There are no rolls, and the plan is never to get assigned. With weekly shorts, the Monday entry already is the roll. A same-bar roll would let a new short bypass the skip gates, and rolling to defer a loss turns a defined loss into an open-ended one. The loss is realized and the next week starts fresh.
Buy the short back once it has lost most of its value: once it's worth {max_credit_fraction:.0%} or less of the credit received.

rules.action: Buy to close at mid. No new short until next Monday
rules.condition: Short delta > {max_delta:.2f}, on any bar
rules.name: Defensive
rules.rationale:
There are no rolls, and the plan is never to get assigned. With weekly shorts, the Monday entry already is the roll. A same-bar roll would let a new short bypass the skip gates, and rolling to defer a loss turns a defined loss into an open-ended one. The loss is realized and the next week starts fresh.
It keeps the short from sitting deep in the money, where early exercise becomes likely.

rules.action: Buy to close at mid
rules.condition: On the week's final session, at the last bar ending at or before {check_by:%H:%M} ET: spot ≥ short strike − {em_buffer:.2f} × EM, with EM measured at the short's entry
rules.name: Friday check
rules.rationale:
There are no rolls, and the plan is never to get assigned. With weekly shorts, the Monday entry already is the roll. A same-bar roll would let a new short bypass the skip gates, and rolling to defer a loss turns a defined loss into an open-ended one. The loss is realized and the next week starts fresh.
The stock can move into the money in the final hour after the check. Treating "within {em_buffer:.2f} × EM of the strike" as in the money reduces missed assignments; X-S5 handles any that still occur, honestly recorded rather than assumed away.

rules.action: EXPIRE at $0
rules.condition: The short is still open at expiry and out of the money at the close (closing spot ≤ strike)
rules.name: Expires out of the money
rules.rationale:
There are no rolls, and the plan is never to get assigned. With weekly shorts, the Monday entry already is the roll. A same-bar roll would let a new short bypass the skip gates, and rolling to defer a loss turns a defined loss into an open-ended one. The loss is realized and the next week starts fresh.
The call expires worthless, and the full credit is kept.

rules.action: ASSIGN the call; open short stock at the strike (Reg T short-stock margin applies); buy to cover at the first valid bar of the next session
rules.condition: The short is still open at expiry and in the money at the close (closing spot > strike)
rules.name: Missed assignment
rules.rationale:
There are no rolls, and the plan is never to get assigned. With weekly shorts, the Monday entry already is the roll. A same-bar roll would let a new short bypass the skip gates, and rolling to defer a loss turns a defined loss into an open-ended one. The loss is realized and the next week starts fresh.
Assignment only happens if the stock jumps into the money after the Friday check, and the backtest records it honestly. The short is never exercised on purpose: buying back an in-the-money short at expiry costs its intrinsic value plus almost no extrinsic, which is economically equal to assignment and covering. Assignment only adds weekend gap risk on short stock, short-stock margin that can push available funds negative, or the loss of the long leg's extrinsic if it's exercised to deliver.

rules.action: Sell long at mid, then re-enter per E-L1 to E-L4 in the same session if E-T1 passes; then apply short-leg entry rules
rules.condition: Long delta < {min_delta:.2f} at the Monday decision bar
rules.name: Long reset
rules.rationale: The long call is the stock substitute, and it's sold and re-bought if its delta falls below {min_delta:.2f}. It's checked on Mondays, before the week's short is sold, so a new short is always covered by the long that's held.

rules.action: Same as X-L1
rules.condition: Long DTE < {min_dte} at the Monday decision bar
rules.name: Long roll
rules.rationale: The long is sold and re-bought once it has fewer than {min_dte} days left, so it stays a long-dated stock substitute. Like X-L1, it's checked on Mondays, before the week's short is sold.

rules.action: Mark all positions to the final bar's mid; no forced liquidation
rules.condition: The window's final bar
rules.name: End of backtest
rules.rationale: Positions are valued at the last price. Nothing is force-closed.

E-L1.action: Buy the E-L2 and E-L3 selection when E-T1 passes. If it doesn't pass this session, retry each following session until it does
E-L1.condition: No long call is held: the window's first session, or a session in which X-L1 or X-L2 sold it
E-L1.rationale: The long call is bought on the first day of the backtest. If no bar in a session passes E-T1, the entry is retried the next session.

E-L2.action: Choose the monthly expiry nearest 180 days to expiry
E-L2.condition: Monthly expiries listed at the decision bar
E-L2.rationale: The textbook PMCC long: a monthly about 180 days out. A listed option with 9 months or less to expiry has no loan value under Reg T, so the long is always fully paid.

E-L3.action: Choose the strike with delta nearest 0.80
E-L3.condition: Eligible calls on the E-L2 expiry
E-L3.rationale: The long call is the stock substitute: a deep in-the-money, long-dated call, here at the textbook PMCC's delta of 0.80.

E-L4.action: Buy a fixed quantity of 1. No entry, logged, if it would make available funds negative. Every account starts with 2× the most expensive first long-leg cost in the universe, rounded up to the nearest $5,000
E-L4.rationale: One long call and one short call. Every symbol's account starts with the same cash balance, used for NAV and Reg T tracking, and no entry is made that would make available funds negative.

E-S1.action: Sell a new short call; E-T1 decides which bar
E-S1.condition: Each Monday (the first session of the week if Monday is a holiday), while a long call is held and no short is open
E-S1.rationale: One short call a week, sold as the week opens. A short closed early isn't replaced until the next Monday, so every new short passes the skip-week gates.

E-S2.action: Use the expiry on that week's final trading session
E-S2.rationale: The short lives for one week. Its expiry is the week's last trading session, so a holiday week never gets an invented Friday expiry: when the Friday is a holiday, it expires on Thursday.

E-S3.action: Choose the strike with delta nearest 0.30
E-S3.condition: Eligible out-of-the-money calls on the E-S2 expiry
E-S3.rationale: The textbook PMCC short: a weekly call out of the money at a fixed delta. If the selected strike fails E-T1 or E-S5, the skip-week gates decide; no other strike is substituted.

E-S4.action: Sell as many contracts as the long leg holds
E-S4.rationale: Each short call is covered by one long call with a lower strike and a later expiry, so the position is a diagonal spread and the short needs no margin of its own under Reg T.

E-S5.action: Sell the short only if this holds; otherwise G-2 skips the week
E-S5.condition: Short strike − long strike > long entry fill − short mid, per share
E-S5.rationale: The gap between the strikes has to be bigger than the net debit paid. Then, if the short finishes deep in the money, the long leg's intrinsic gain covers the short's loss plus the debit, so the trade still doesn't lose money overall. It uses the long leg's entry fill, not its current mark, which keeps it conservative.

E-T1.action: Enter the long on the first bar of the session where the condition holds. Decide the short only on session bar 1 of the week-open session (bar 1 ends at 10:00): sell it if the condition holds there, or else G-1 skips the week
E-T1.condition: The selected contract has a valid bid and ask, and its spread is at most 3% of mid for the long leg or 10% for the short leg
E-T1.rationale: The entry-timing check: the baseline with E-T1's liquidity trigger replaced by a fixed bar of the week-open session, run once for each of its bars. Large dispersion in results across the bars is reported as fragility.

G-1.action: Skip the week; keep the long
G-1.condition: Selected short never passes E-T1 on any Monday bar
G-1.rationale: No tradable quote, no trade: the backtest never invents a fill and never swaps in a different strike. G-1 replaces a separate short-leg spread gate, since E-T1's spread threshold already covers it.

G-2.action: Skip the week; keep the long
G-2.rationale: A short that could turn the position into a net loss isn't sold, and no other strike is tried in its place.

X-E1.action: Mark all positions to the final bar's mid; no forced liquidation
X-E1.rationale: Positions are valued at the last price. Nothing is force-closed.

X-L1.action: Sell long at mid, then re-enter per E-L1 to E-L4 in the same session if E-T1 passes; then apply short-leg entry rules
X-L1.condition: Long delta < 0.50 at the Monday decision bar
X-L1.rationale: The long call is the stock substitute, and it's sold and re-bought if its delta falls below 0.50. It's checked on Mondays, before the week's short is sold, so a new short is always covered by the long that's held.

X-L2.condition: Long DTE < 90 at the Monday decision bar
X-L2.rationale: The long is sold and re-bought once it has fewer than 90 days left, so it stays a long-dated stock substitute. Like X-L1, it's checked on Mondays, before the week's short is sold.

X-S1.action: Buy to close at mid. No new short until next Monday
X-S1.condition: Short mid ≤ 25% of the credit received, on any bar before the Friday check
X-S1.rationale:
There are no rolls, and the plan is never to get assigned. With weekly shorts, the Monday entry already is the roll. A same-bar roll would let a new short bypass the skip gates, and rolling to defer a loss turns a defined loss into an open-ended one. The loss is realized and the next week starts fresh.
Buy the short back once it has lost most of its value: once it's worth 25% or less of the credit received.

X-S2.rationale:
There are no rolls, and the plan is never to get assigned. With weekly shorts, the Monday entry already is the roll. A same-bar roll would let a new short bypass the skip gates, and rolling to defer a loss turns a defined loss into an open-ended one. The loss is realized and the next week starts fresh.
It keeps the short from sitting deep in the money, where early exercise becomes likely.

X-S3.condition: On the week's final session, at the last bar ending at or before 15:00 ET: spot ≥ short strike − 0.25 × EM, with EM measured at the short's entry
X-S3.rationale:
There are no rolls, and the plan is never to get assigned. With weekly shorts, the Monday entry already is the roll. The stock can move into the money in the final hour after the check. Treating "within 0.25 × EM of the strike" as in the money reduces missed assignments; X-S5 handles any that still occur, honestly recorded rather than assumed away.

X-S4.condition: The short is still open at expiry and out of the money at the close (closing spot ≤ strike)
X-S4.rationale:
There are no rolls, and the plan is never to get assigned. With weekly shorts, the Monday entry already is the roll. A same-bar roll would let a new short bypass the skip gates, and rolling to defer a loss turns a defined loss into an open-ended one. The loss is realized and the next week starts fresh.
The call expires worthless, and the full credit is kept.

X-S5.condition: The short is still open at expiry and in the money at the close (closing spot > strike)
X-S5.rationale:
